title: Psalms Bible Quiz - Chapter 143
description: Ten questions on Psalms 143: a servant's plea, a soul thirsty like parched land, and a prayer to be taught God's will.

questions.text: Why does the psalmist ask God not to enter into judgment with his servant?
questions.explanation: He says, "Don't enter into judgment with your servant, for in your sight no man living is righteous."

answers.text: God's anger lasts only a moment
The servant has already been punished
In God's sight no man living is righteous

questions.text: Where has the enemy made the psalmist live?
questions.explanation: The enemy has struck his life down to the ground and made him live in dark places, as those who have been long dead.

answers.text: In a dry and weary land without any water
In dark places, as those who have been long dead
In the tents of the wicked far from home
In a city besieged on every side

questions.text: What does the psalmist do with the days of old?
questions.explanation: He says, "I remember the days of old. I meditate on all your doings."

answers.text: He remembers them and meditates on all God's doings
He mourns over them with fasting and weeping
He asks God to blot them out of his memory
He writes them down in a book of remembrance

questions.text: What does the psalmist compare his thirsty soul to?
questions.explanation: He spreads out his hands to God and says his soul thirsts for him like a parched land.

questions.text: If God hides his face, the psalmist fears he will become like whom?
questions.explanation: He asks God not to hide his face, so that he does not become like those who go down into the pit.

answers.text: A sparrow alone on a roof
Those who go down into the pit

questions.text: What does the psalmist ask to hear in the morning?
questions.explanation: He prays, "Cause me to hear your loving kindness in the morning, for I trust in you."

answers.text: The voice of his accusers silenced

questions.text: What does the psalmist say he does when he asks to be delivered from his enemies?
questions.explanation: He prays, "Deliver me, Yahweh, from my enemies. I flee to you to hide me."

answers.text: He takes up shield and armor
He flees to God to hide him

questions.text: What does the psalmist ask God to teach him?
questions.explanation: He prays, "Teach me to do your will, for you are my God. Your Spirit is good."

questions.text: For whose sake does the psalmist ask Yahweh to revive him?
questions.explanation: He prays, "Revive me, Yahweh, for your name's sake. In your righteousness, bring my soul out of trouble."

answers.text: For the sake of the fathers

questions.text: What reason does the psalmist give when he asks God to cut off his enemies?
questions.explanation: He asks God in his loving kindness to cut off his enemies and destroy those who afflict his soul, "For I am your servant."

answers.text: He has kept all the commandments
